extracted.intended_audience: Area Chairs (ACs) for ACL Rolling Review (ARR) / ACL venues
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for Area Chairs handling paper assignment, monitoring review quality, managing reviewer-author interactions, and writing meta-reviews within the ACL Rolling Review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest / expertise check
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether you happen to know the paper and have a conflict of interest with it, or feel that it is completely out of your field of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it happens, reach out to your SAC and request a reassignment immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactly three reviewers assigned
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper has to have exactly three reviewers assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the initial stage, do not assign more than three reviewers to a paper. In large cycles we cannot afford to waste reviewers' effort. Use search +numReviewersAssigned>3 to detect over-assignment and remove assignments if you add another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer maximum load compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not be assigned more papers than their maximum load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 'modify reviewer assignments' to see each reviewer's 'max papers' and 'assignments'. If a reviewer exceeds max, find replacement reviewers under their maximum load. Do not assign reviewers already at max load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer seniority requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one (ideally two) of the reviewers is past the postgraduate degree stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Seniority flag (should be 1 for non-students). Note past bugs with this flag; interpret carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer diversity in affiliation and geography
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigned reviewers should be diverse in terms of affiliation and geography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewer profiles and affiliations shown in the assignment interface to assess diversity; respect this criterion as much as possible given the reviewer pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission reviewer continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions, the same past reviewers should be assigned unless the authors requested new reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify resubmissions via 'Previous URL' link in Supplementary Materials. If original reviewers are available and not at max capacity, assign them. If at max, attempt to shift assignments within your batch or contact original reviewers to request they review the resubmission; if impossible, replace with new reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling desk-rejected previous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that some previous submissions were desk rejected (comments at top of forum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If desk rejection was due to anonymity violations, avoid looking at the previous pdf to not accidentally discover author identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the AC checklist — scope appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify whether the paper is appropriate for ACL venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, consider the ARR CFP and CFPs of conferences associated with the review cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the AC checklist — formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the paper is properly formatted according to the ACL guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACL has separate LaTeX and Microsoft Word templates; PDFs produced by these templates look different. Check against ACL templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the AC checklist — page length
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the paper has the proper length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short papers: 4 content pages maximum. Long papers: 8 content pages maximum. Sections on ethical considerations and limitations do not count towards page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the AC checklist — Limitations section
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the paper has a section entitled 'Limitations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of a Limitations section is explicitly checked in the AC checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the AC checklist — anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the paper is properly anonymized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TLDR: no clear self-citations, acknowledgements, or non-anonymous repository links. Resources shouldn’t be linked from services like Dropbox which may track who opened the links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the AC checklist — Responsible Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the Responsible Checklist is filled appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egregious violations (e.g., saying 'yes' to all inapplicable questions or missing required justifications) may qualify for desk rejection starting December 2024; minor honest mistakes may be excused.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC checklist — presence of 3 reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm that the submission has 3 reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We cannot afford more than 3 reviewers; remove an assignment if you add another reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC checklist — ethics review flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the paper should be sent for an in-depth ethics review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If so, provide justification. Refer to 'Guidelines for ethics review flagging'. Ethics review runs in parallel — AC flagging is necessary to start the process on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of reviewer affinity scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Affinity scores reflect content matching of the reviewer's own papers with the submission; aggregate scores incorporate affinity, track matching, and other criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: [3] = paper is a resubmission and authors request same reviewers (do not change); [1,2] = paper track matches reviewer-specified track; (0,1) = reviewer's track doesn't match paper track; 0 = paper is a resubmission and authors requested new reviewers (these reviewers are not to be assigned). Pay special attention to generic tracks like 'NLP Applications' and 'Machine Learning for NLP' — automated matching may be poor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: do NOT actively search for the paper title online
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither ACs nor reviewers should actively seek non-anonymized versions of the papers they are reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identity is discovered, reviewers should request reassignment or disclose in the review form; whenever possible honor such reassignment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing review checks — monitor incoming reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Check in periodically as reviews come in and react to any low-quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a review needs improvement, contact the reviewer via an official comment (with SACs in the loop). Junior reviewers may be willing to improve given specific guidance. If non-responsive, proceed with emergency reassignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not unassign unreliable reviewers when adding replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need to replace a reviewer because they might be unreliable, do not unassign them when you add a new reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete reviews are one mechanism to identify unreliable reviewers; keep the original assignment for record and statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common review problems to spot
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface-level indicators of low-quality reviews that ACs should detect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one-liner reviews; rude reviews; low scores not accompanied by substantial criticism; blanket non-specific statements (e.g., 'not novel' without references, 'too few experiments' without specifics); misuse of heuristics; content that appears LLM-generated or not based on sufficient understanding. Neither reviewers nor ACs are supposed to rely on LLMs for content; using commercial LLMs even for language checking violates confidentiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request fixes or emergency reassignments for problematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If obvious problems exist in reviews, ask reviewers to fix specific issues; if non-responsive, bring in emergency reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For serious malpractice where a review should be removed, add an official comment addressed to chairs and authors with text: 'This review does not meet the ARR quality standards, and will be disregarded in the assessment' and specify in meta-review or review rating form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review chasing — handling late or unresponsive reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Chase late reviewers and manage replacements so papers end up with three reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact late reviewers (email is more effective). If they will not submit in time or are unresponsive, bring in emergency reviewers. Each unresponsive reviewer should have exactly one replacement. Many cycles are at max capacity, so avoid multiple replacements per paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding emergency reviewers — three approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Ways to find and invite emergency reviewers when replacements are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Find reviewers on OpenReview, email them first, then use 'invite assignment' only for the one who answers. 2) Reach out to volunteers on BlueSky or other social networks. 3) Reach out to people in your own network; offer to give feedback to junior reviewers. When adding someone not in the reviewer pool, you can add them yourself. Add only one extra reviewer to avoid ending up with 6 reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep record of removed/unresponsive reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not remove the unresponsive reviewer (their status is collected for ARR statistics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to decrease caps or delete old invitations, do so carefully (trash can button).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify reviewers when assignments change
rubrics_metrics.description: If you modify any assignments after they have been sent to reviewers, you must notify the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OpenReview does not automatically notify reviewers when ACs change assignments. Use personal email or official comments to inform them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-author discussion moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: During the discussion period authors drive the discussion; reviewers are encouraged to at least acknowledge responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discussion becomes openly hostile or unprofessional, step in and remind participants about the ACL anti-harassment policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review should summarize reviews, discussions, and author response
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-review is a summary that states the most prominent strengths and weaknesses and explicitly judges whether strengths outweigh weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should help authors understand what revision to aim for and help chairs make accept/reject decisions. Meta-reviews should be specific (especially about recommended revisions) and professional in tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review scoring scale and backing text
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR metareview score options and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New options (Feb 2025): 5 = Consider for Award; 4.5 = Borderline Award; 4.0 = Conference; 3.5 = Borderline Conference; 3 = Findings; 2.5 = Borderline Findings; 2 = Resubmit next cycle; 1.5 = Resubmit after next cycle; 1 = Do not resubmit. Like reviews, the score should be backed up by the meta-review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewer scores of soundness, excitement, and overall
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR reviewers are asked to provide three scores: soundness, excitement, and overall recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All papers recommended for Findings or main conference are expected to be sound and reproducible. ACs should mostly follow reviewers' soundness assessment when reviewers agree, and can weigh in when there is disagreement or serious issues with reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main conference vs Findings distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria distinguishing main conference vs Findings recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection among good papers considers which are distinguished by excitement, novelty, impact, and/or other factors. Reviewer excitement is neither necessary nor sufficient; consider case-by-case. Improvements in efficiency or high-quality resources may justify main track despite modest novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: If not recommending, state clear required work
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not recommend the paper for main conference or Findings, the meta-review should clearly signal what work is required to be publication-ready.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are two tiers for resubmission recommendations depending on amount of work needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of reasons to publish must reflect reviewers' acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Summary of reasons to publish' should not be just authors' claimed contributions but those acknowledged by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present contributions that reviewers accept as valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of suggested revisions must be clear and actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Summary of suggested revisions' should list clear revisions you expect authors to address in a resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about priorities and the nature of required work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging papers for ethics during meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you strongly believe a big ethical problem was missed earlier, provide this information during meta-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While ethics should be flagged at AC checklist stage, if missed, still report; ARR is developing a process for late flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating outstanding papers
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs may nominate papers to be considered by the best paper committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outstanding papers should be fascinating, controversial, surprising, impressive, or potentially field-changing. Up to 2.5% of papers may receive 'outstanding' awards; awards decided on camera-ready versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of information for meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary sources are reviews, author response, and reported review issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider author response and reported review issues (I1-I12). Read at least 2 author responses per review thread. If authors flagged problems, judge whether complaints are reasonable and indicate in meta-review checkboxes whether you took them into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling reported review issues (I1-I12)
rubrics_metrics.description: During author response authors can flag problematic reviews with issue codes I1-I12; ACs must consider such complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most reported issues are mentioned in reviewer guidelines. If complaint is reasonable, state that you took issues into account in the meta-review or that you did not find them justified. If multiple issues reported and some justified and some not, check both checkboxes in the meta-review form. You may also provide a brief response to authors in a dedicated text field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding new criticisms as ACs
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs may add new information/criticisms to the meta-review when they believe reviewers overlooked something crucial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only do so when strongly necessary; substantiate any new issues and mark them transparently (e.g., 'AC note: ___'). Mention other developments (e.g., reviewer consensus) you observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewer discussion to resolve disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers disagree strongly, initiate reviewer-only discussion to encourage consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post official comment with reviewers and chairs as readers (not authors); specify the exact point(s) to be discussed. Discussions can be used before or after author response. It's OK if differences remain provided you understand their rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewer discussion to determine revision priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use discussion to get reviewers to agree on top priorities for revision when there are many suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List top opportunities for improvement and ask reviewers whether they'd raise their score for a revision satisfying those points. Consider page limit constraints for resubmissions and ask reviewers what can be removed to make space or whether to switch formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on AC use of AI assistants
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-reviews, discussions and reviews are confidential materials and should not be submitted to non-privacy-preserving third-party services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of privacy-preserving tools is governed by ACL publication ethics policy: permissible for language/input assistance but you are fully responsible for content. If automated summaries miss key aspects, responsibility lies with you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting great reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: List reviewers who went beyond expectations as 'great reviewers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of desired service: rigorous reviewers (examining code/data, reporting hard-to-spot issues), high-quality emergency reviewers, champion reviewers who defend a paper, open-minded reviewers, patient reviewers. List forum IDs in meta-review form or flag directly on the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting unacceptable reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag reviews that provide exceptionally bad service or violate guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include rude reviews, guideline or procedural violations, going MIA without notification, LLM-generated reviews. You can list them in meta-review form or flag directly on the review. For reviews that should be removed, add the specified official comment and list them in meta-review fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms for reporting great/unacceptable reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Two reporting mechanisms are available to ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Through the meta-review form (text fields for forum IDs). 2) Flagging directly on the review via a new form on the review. Senior area chairs and program chairs will have similar forms for meta-reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling papers with late reviews when reviews released
rubrics_metrics.description: If some papers still miss reviews when reviews are released, consider enabling authors to submit a reply and nudging reviewers to update their assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are not obligated to do this; check dates when reviews were posted. If logistically possible, you may wait to submit meta-reviews for these papers until author-reviewer engagement is over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-reviewing resubmissions — focus on past concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: When meta-reviewing resubmissions, focus on how past essential concerns were addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors requested same reviewers, they should assess how adequately the major concerns were addressed. Do not penalize sincere efforts to address weaknesses. Exception: if revisions result in contradictory findings or questionable results not present earlier, that is a problem. Reviewers substituting for original reviewers form their own view and may raise new issues that should receive due consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission citation comparison requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmitted papers are required to make comparisons to highly related relevant work published at least three months prior to the original submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are encouraged to discuss contemporaneous work where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview procedural responsibility — contacting SACs/Reviewers/EiCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the AC console and Official Comment functionality to contact SACs, reviewers, and EiCs; be professional and polite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reasonable timeframes for replies. To contact a SAC for a specific paper, use 'Add Official Comment' with SACs as readers. To contact reviewers, use Official Comment, the 'Message' checkbox, or obtain reviewers' email addresses and reach out directly. Notifications from OpenReview go to reviewers' emails; sometimes responses happen by email and may be routed to ARR support, so be mindful.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview account/profile hygiene for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage reviewers to maintain accurate OpenReview profiles so matching is effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating accounts, fill in Semantic Scholar URL, DBLP, ACL Anthology, education, advisor, expertise keywords (specific, not generic). Reviewers should delete unrelated papers and those they didn't author to improve matching.
